issues.legal_issue: Property received by a son from his father by gift or bequest does not become ancestral property merely because it came from his father.
material_facts: The father held the relevant properties as his self-acquired property.
The son received the properties under his father's will, rather than by inheritance or partition.
The claim for partition depended on treating the properties as ancestral in the son's hands.
issues.conclusion: A property gifted or bequeathed by a father to his son does not become ancestral in the son's hands merely because the son received it from his father; the interest taken depends on the grant's terms and the donor's intention.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Mitakshara, including Chapter 1, section 4, placita 1 and 28, a father's gift is a distinct category of property exempt from partition, and the son's interest in property received by gift or bequest depends on the grantor's intention. The mode of transmission matters: property ordinarily becomes ancestral when received by descent as a son or descendant, not simply because it is granted by an ancestor. The Court relied on Rao Balwant v. Rani Kishori for the father's power over his self-acquired property and considered Muddun v. Ram and the conflicting High Court authorities; Lal Ram Singh v. Deputy Commissioner, Partabgarh had left the question open.

predicates.property_character_dispute: A party to a dispute over property character claims rights on the basis that the property is ancestral.
predicates.father_transferred_property_by_gift_or_b: A father transferred property to a son by gift or testamentary bequest.
predicates.recipient_received_property_by_grant_not: The son received the property by the father's grant rather than through inheritance by descent.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns whether property granted by a father to a son is ancestral, receipt by grant rather than descent does not by itself make the property ancestral.

issues.legal_issue: The terms of a will and the surrounding circumstances determine whether property bequeathed by a father is given to a son absolutely or for the benefit of the son's family.
material_facts: The testator stated that the properties were his own acquisitions and allocated different properties to his three sons and other relatives.
The will gave the sons absolute rights and powers to sell, gift, or exchange their allotted properties.
The will made provisions for the testator's wife and other relatives and did not give the properties to the sons' male descendants.
The arrangements differed from the shares that would have resulted from a partition under Hindu law.
The other properties claimed as joint family property were said to be accretions to the bequeathed properties.
issues.conclusion: The will showed that the sons received the bequeathed properties absolutely as their separate property, not as ancestral property for their branches; the appeal was allowed and the partition suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Where a grant does not clearly describe the interest conveyed, the court determines the donor's intention from the document's language and surrounding circumstances, applying established canons of construction and considering the substance rather than the form of the disposition. The material question is whether the donor intended an individual bounty or a disposition that was in substance part of a partition. There is no presumption that the donor intended either a gift or a partition, because a father may choose either course.

rule.if: partition_suit and grantor_owned_property_separately and will_grants_absolute_rights and will_authorizes_alienation and will_makes_provisions_for_other_relatives and will_allocates_property_differently_from_partition_shares

predicates.partition_suit: A claimant brings a suit seeking partition on the ground that property belongs to the family jointly.
predicates.grantor_owned_property_separately: The testator held the property as his own acquisition rather than as joint family property.
predicates.will_grants_absolute_rights: The testator's will states that the sons are to hold their allotted properties absolutely.
predicates.will_authorizes_alienation: The will authorizes the sons to sell, gift, or exchange the properties allotted to them.
predicates.will_makes_provisions_for_other_relative: The will separately provides property or benefits for relatives other than the sons.
predicates.will_allocates_property_differently_from: The will's allocation differs from the shares that would have been given in a partition under the applicable family rules.

issues.definition: When a partition suit concerns separately owned property allocated by a will that grants absolute rights and permits alienation, and the will makes separate provisions for other relatives in an allocation unlike partition shares, the property is held separately by the legatee.
